title: incident-bot: oncall autodiagnostics workflow enhancements (ranked runbooks, telemetry links, UX hints)
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Enhances oncall autodiagnostics workflow: ranked runbook suggestions, direct telemetry/dashboard quicklinks, UX hinting for triage steps, and improved unit test coverage.
body:
Background: oncall engineers rely on the incident-bot autodiagnostics to surface likely root-cause signals and runbook links during SLO-triggered alerts. Current suggestions are useful but noisy: runbooks are unordered, telemetry links are buried, and some actionable hints are missing. This PR improves the diagnostics workflow to reduce time-to-mitigation and increase signal-to-noise for oncall.

What this change does (high level): - Add a ranked runbook suggestion pipeline that scores candidate runbooks by estimated SLO impact, recent similarity of incidents, and playbook freshness. - Surface direct telemetry/dashboard quicklinks (Grafana/Datadog) alongside each suggestion with prefilled time ranges based on incident start time. - Add concise UX hints (one-line triage actions) derived from runbook metadata (e.g., "check service X pod restarts", "inspect queue depth metric"). - Refactor autodiag core to separate scoring from presentation (prepares for future model-backed ranking). - Expand unit and integration tests and add end-to-end telemetry link tests. - Minor frontend adjustments to RunbookSuggestions component: improved loading states, keyboard focus for quicklinks, and copy-to-clipboard for commands.

Implementation notes: - New components: src/autodiag/ranker.py (scoring logic), src/autodiag/telemetry_links.py (dashboard link generator), src/ui/runbook_suggestions.tsx (presentation updates). - Scoring uses a weighted heuristic: signal_match_score (50%), recent_incident_similarity (30%), runbook_recency_penalty (10%), manual_priority_override (10%). We experimented with an ML-ranker stub but kept deterministic heuristics for this rollout. - Telemetry links support Grafana and Datadog; customers without configured targets fall back to a discovery link. - Added feature flag ONCALL_AUTODIAG_RANKING to toggle ranking during rollout.

Testing and rollout: - Added unit tests for ranking logic and telemetry link formatting. - E2E test that simulates a synthetic SLO alert and verifies top-3 runbook suggestions, presence of telemetry links, and that hint strings include expected keywords. - Feature gated; rollout plan: enable for internal staging, run canary for 48h on high-severity SLO alerts, monitor MTTI and suggestion acceptance metrics before broader ramp.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear ENG-4821 - [x] Unit tests added - [x] E2E telemetry link test added - [x] Feature flag implemented - [x] Metrics/tracing hooks added - [x] Updated oncall docs (docs/oncall/autodiag.md)

Motivation and impact: Oncall survey and postmortem analysis showed that explicit telemetry links and ordered runbook suggestions would reduce initial triage time. This change should reduce average time-to-first-action for SLO alerts and reduce pager fatigue by surfacing higher-value runbooks first.
